event.label: reported
event.text: Ahead of the November 5 strike, Ouest-France reported that about 250 rallies were planned across France at the unions' call, with train, metro and public-transport services expected to be disrupted in the main cities.

event.label: disputed
event.text: France's Interior Ministry said more than 600,000 people marched on November 5 for higher wages and in support of the school protest movement, while the CGT union said nearly 1.6 million took part in over 200 demonstrations, the Associated Press reported. ICI reported that at 1pm the interior minister's office counted 270,000 people at 180 rallies outside Paris, with 70,000 police and gendarmes deployed.

event.label: alleged
event.text: The FSU teachers' union said on Bluesky and Instagram that the strike was a majority one in lower and upper secondary schools (52% of collège teachers, it said in a video) and that nearly 1.6 million people marched; the CGT said on Telegram that 1.6 million were mobilised. Both unions urged further action. These are the unions' own figures.

event.label: disputed
event.text: Local counts differed from the unions' on November 5: the Sarthe prefect said 8,700 marched in Le Mans with no incidents while organisers estimated about 10,000, Ouest-France reported; in Cherbourg-en-Cotentin police counted 3,300 and unions 3,600 despite a prefectural ban; and the Côtes-d'Armor prefecture reported at least 8,400 marchers, with no violence.

event.label: reported
event.text: Lycée students blocked schools in several towns on November 5, including about 150 pupils at one school in Valence, ICI reported, and several lycées in Sarthe, Ouest-France reported.

event.label: reported
event.text: About thirty masked people entered the Lycée Françoise in Tournefeuille, near Toulouse, at around 7:40 a.m. on November 5 and set fires and caused heavy damage, Le Monde reported. No pupils were in the school, and local officials condemned the attack.
